note: The hand-kept part of the Machines catalogue (schema/MACHINE_CATALOGUE.md): what each kind of machine is and does, which group it stands in, which species' records name it, and where its size, count and proteins are read. tools/build_catalogue.py reads this file, the species files, the species' own proteins and the machine files, and writes data/catalogue/catalogue.json. No number is written here that a source does not give, and no sentence of a paper but the one quoted with its place. The membrane units of the law inventory are not listed here: the page reads them from the scene's protein units, as the Protein atlas does.
decided: The tab and its catalogue were asked for on 17 November 2026: a catalogue of molecular machines by species, gathered as the proteins were, in a design of its own. Decided 17 November 2026 (D209): the tab is the first milestone (M0) of the engine's path for machines, a catalogue with drawing levels labelled illustration; no machine is in the engine, and the drawing levels are the viewer's, not simulation detail. The coordinator ruled the same evening that a machine keeps one identity on the page.

groups.label: Making proteins
groups.plain: Machines that read a messenger RNA and build the protein it codes for.

groups.label: Reading genes
groups.plain: Machines that copy a gene's DNA into RNA.

groups.label: Making ATP
groups.plain: Machines that make the cell's fuel from a flow of ions across a membrane.

groups.label: Moving ions: units of the law inventory
groups.plain: Channels, pumps, exchangers and junctions: the units of the engine's law inventory that are protein assemblies, as the Protein atlas lists them. A unit's panel says which of its laws an active model declares.

groups.label: Putting proteins into membranes
groups.plain: Channels that thread new proteins across a membrane or set them into it.

groups.label: Breaking proteins down
groups.plain: Proteases that unfold proteins and cut them, using ATP.

groups.label: Moving, sensing and attaching
groups.plain: Machines that move the cell, steer it, or hold it to a surface.

fr13.label: FR-13, Molecular machines, individually and in aggregate

d209.label: D209, Molecular machines: M0 now, then M1

cell-structures.label: The Cell view's structures
cell-structures.where: What each status rests on: Ribosomes

units_left_out.note: Units of the law inventory that the catalogue does not hold, because they are not protein assemblies: a leak, a permeability, a lumped conductance, or a law that names no protein. The Protein atlas keeps all its units.

units.unit.U18: a generic delayed-rectifier current that names no protein
units.unit.U46: a transporter configured in a run, that names no protein
units.unit.U47: a passive permeability of the mitochondrial inner membrane

kinds.label: Ribosome
kinds.plain: Reads a messenger RNA and joins amino acids, one at a time, into the protein it codes for.

kinds.label: RNA polymerase
kinds.plain: Copies a gene's DNA into RNA, the first step from a gene to a protein.

kinds.label: ATP synthase
kinds.plain: Turns as ions flow through it across a membrane, and makes ATP as it turns; run the other way, it spends ATP to pump ions out.

records.says: Decided 17 November 2026 (D209): the ATP synthase is to be the first machine built in the engine (M1), as general pieces, after the core-seams pass; its law is to be D193's proton_coupled_atp_synthesis_cycle@1, built by the mitochondria lane. There is no model of it yet.

kinds.label: Protein translocon
kinds.plain: A channel in the membrane that threads a new protein across it, or opens sideways to set it into the membrane.

kinds.label: FtsH protease
kinds.plain: A protease that stands in the cell membrane and unfolds and cuts proteins, using ATP.

kinds.label: Lon protease
kinds.plain: A protease that unfolds and cuts proteins inside the cell, using ATP.

kinds.label: HslUV protease
kinds.plain: A barrel of HslV that cuts proteins, capped by a ring of HslU that unfolds them and feeds them in, using ATP. HslV's subunits carry the signature of the proteasome's.

kinds.label: Chemoreceptor array
kinds.plain: A lattice of receptor proteins in the membrane that senses chemicals and steers the cell's swimming toward food.

kinds.label: Attachment organelle
kinds.plain: A membrane protrusion at one pole with an internal core: it carries the adhesins that hold the cell to a surface, and leads the cell when it glides.

count.says: one at the foot of each flagellum

measures.note: Sizes measured by the viewer from a Protein Data Bank entry's coordinates with tools/measure_particle.py: the tool's own output, kept here as written. A species' file that states a part's size of its own (cell.parts.ribosome) is read first, and the measure here is then not used. The Protein Data Bank states no size: each number is the viewer's own.

ecoli-rna-polymerase.note: the σ70 holoenzyme, with no DNA

ecoli-translocon.note: SecYEG alone, measured from an entry where it holds YidC and sits on a ribosome, both left out; only about half of SecG's sequence stands in its coordinates

ecoli-hslv.note: HslV's barrel of twelve capped by one HslU ring of six, the crystal's biological assembly; capped at both ends beside it

pdb6p1k.text: Protein Data Bank entry 6P1K: Cryo-EM structure of Escherichia coli sigma70 bound RNAP polymerase holoenzyme. Electron microscopy, 4.05 Å; Escherichia coli, by the entry's own source records.

pdb9rbf.text: Protein Data Bank entry 9RBF: Structure of a stalled E. coli 70S RNC-NuoK-86 in complex with the membrane protein insertase SecYEG-YidC. Electron microscopy, 2.44 Å; Escherichia coli, by the entry's own source records.

pdb1g4a.text: Protein Data Bank entry 1G4A: Crystal structures of the HslVU peptidase-ATPase complex reveal an ATP-dependent proteolysis mechanism. X-ray diffraction, 3.0 Å; its first biological assembly; Escherichia coli, by the entry's own source records.

pdb1g4b.text: Protein Data Bank entry 1G4B: Crystal structures of the HslVU peptidase-ATPase complex reveal an ATP-dependent proteolysis mechanism. X-ray diffraction, 7.0 Å; its first biological assembly; Escherichia coli, by the entry's own source records.

pdb6u5z.text: Protein Data Bank entry 6U5Z: Cryo-EM structure of E. coli LonA S679A. Electron microscopy, 3.5 Å; Escherichia coli, by the entry's own source records.

pdb7k00.text: Protein Data Bank entry 7K00: Structure of the Bacterial Ribosome at 2 Angstrom Resolution. Electron microscopy, 1.98 Å; Escherichia coli, strain MRE600, by the entry's own source records.

pdb5mdz.text: Protein Data Bank entry 5MDZ: Structure of the 70S ribosome (empty A site). Electron microscopy, 3.10 Å; Escherichia coli, by the entry's own source records.
